name: # Johnny 5 master parameter sheet. Single source of truth for all build scripts.
# locked=1 values come from the approved BOM / Phase 00 handoff and must not change without a phase decision.
# locked=0 values are design choices made during Task 7 and may be tuned.
track_thickness
note: TPU track band thickness (raises axle line above pitch circle)

name: track_cc
column7: confirmed Session 02)

name: idler_dia
note: Front idler outer dia (matches sprocket for level top run)

name: roadwheel_dia
note: Road-wheel outer dia (supports TPU track between sprocket and idler)

name: roadwheel_pitch
note: Road-wheel centre-to-centre. At the old wheelbase*0.6 formula two ø24 wheels landed 24 mm apart and touched. 40 mm spaces the four ground-contact points evenly along the 119.4 mm run and leaves 8 mm to the sprocket and 7.4 mm to the idler

name: axle_hole_dia
note: Side-wall through-hole for the 3 mm idler and road-wheel shafts

name: idler_axle_dia
note: Idler shaft dia; one full-width rod through both walls so it cannot cock

name: motor_fit_clear
note: Diametral clearance on the motor bore and drop-in slot (0.4 was a press fit at printed tolerance; the cap preloads the motor down so a looser bore is free)

name: motor_insert_margin
note: Axial clearance in the motor pocket. The shaft no longer passes through the wall (the sprocket rides its own bearing) so this is drop-in and wiring room
column7: not slide travel

name: motor_conn_relief_d
note: Depth of the connector relief into the -Y pocket wall; height of the Pololu 5218 back connector where it stands proud of the can

name: motor_conn_relief_l
note: Length of the connector relief from the pocket's inboard end; the travel needed to seat the shaft fully through the sprocket

name: drive_bearing_od
note: Drive hub bearing OD; sets the rear-wall seat diameter

name: drive_bearing_w
note: Drive hub bearing width; seat depth from the wall outer face

name: drive_hub_od
note: Stepped hub outer dia riding the bearing; bored 3 mm for the motor shaft

name: drive_boss_t
note: Material inboard of the wall reserved for the bearing seat shoulder; the motor front face stops this far short of the wall inner face

name: motor_cap_t
note: Retention cap plate thickness above the cradle top

name: motor_cap_screw_cc
note: Cap screw spacing across the motor axis (Y); sets cradle width

name: motor_cap_screw_x
note: Cap screw spacing along the motor axis (X)

name: motor_cap_screw_depth
note: Tapped depth into the cradle for the cap screws

name: motor_cap_clamp_gap
note: Preload gap so the cap seats on the motor before the cradle top

name: motor_cap_fit
note: Slip fit between the cap tongue and the cradle slot; must exceed motor_fit_clear/2 or the tongue ends up wider than the motor and the saddle stops gripping

name: motor_cap_wall_clear
note: Cap-to-tub-wall clearance; the cap is a separate part and cannot merge into the walls the way the cradle does

name: tub_wall
note: Tub wall (6 perimeters @0.4); load zones thicker via bosses

name: tub_width
note: Tub outer width (sits 2mm inside inner track faces)

name: battery_bay_aft_clear
note: Gap between the bay ring's aft face and the motor cradle. The ring used to run past the cradle and block both hand access and the motor's rear wire exit

name: pi_shelf_z
note: Shelf height above tub floor (above battery)

name: pi_rib_x_in
note: Support column inner face; must sit outboard of the battery bay ring or the pack cannot seat

name: pi_shelf_half_w
note: Shelf plate half-width; must reach past the rib centreline far enough to seat an M2 head

name: pi_shelf_aft_half_w
note: Half-width of the plate's aft tail
column7: from the motor cradle face back. At full width the tail roofed both retention caps and one cap screw each -- a buried fastener of exactly the kind the IMU was moved off the tub floor to avoid. Steps in to clear the cap footprint by 0.9 mm and still carry the breadboard standoffs with 1.1 mm to spare

name: pi_shelf_screw_inset
note: Retained for the aft column inset from the plate edge

name: pi_shelf_aft_ext
note: How much further aft the shelf runs than a Pi-only plate. Carries the IMU breadboard: one electronics shelf that can be built up outside the tub and dropped in. Set by the aft stack -- 4.1 mm behind the Pi board
column7: 50.8 mm of breadboard

name: pi_shelf_t
note: Shelf plate thickness. Was 2.0 hardcoded; a 111 mm plate now carrying the IMU wants the extra

name: pi_columns_per_side
note: Support columns replacing the two solid ribs. The ribs were 8.4 x 73 mm walls; extending them to 111 mm would have cost 58 g
column7: and columns take that to 23 g

name: pi_column_cradle_clear
note: Gap the aft support column leaves in front of the motor cradle. The shelf runs back over the cradles now; a column at the plate's aft edge would stand inside the motor drop-in pocket
column7: so the aft column stops here and the plate cantilevers the rest

name: pi_wire_slot_w
column7: between the Pi board edge and the columns

name: pi_loom_slot_w
note: Aft loom slot width; battery and motor wiring up from the floor

name: # The band was smooth on the ground side. Treads are cut INTO the 3.5 mm

value: which halves the outer-fibre bending strain

tread_depth
note: Tread relief depth; valley radius 22.0 against a 23.5 tip

name: tread_rib_w
note: Rib thickness along the path; 8+ extrusions wide at a 0.4 nozzle so it prints solid

name: tread_count
note: Chevrons around the loop. 15.7 mm pitch puts 7.6 of them in ground contact per side
column7: so contact never steps

name: tread_segments
note: Segments per chevron arm. A straight arm laid tangentially on the 22 mm valley radius floats 1.6 mm of each end clear of the band on every curved section and stands 1.36 mm proud of the tip radius; following the path in short steps drops that to 0.2 mm

name: tread_angle
note: Chevron arm angle from transverse. Gives lateral bite in tank turns; the loop prints with its width vertical so this is also the arm's lean off vertical
column7: well inside self-supporting

name: imu_board_w
note: Solderable mini breadboard X extent. The IMU is not screwed to the shelf directly any more -- it rides this board so the sensor and its connectors can be soldered up and tested off the robot

name: imu_hole_cc_x
note: Breadboard mount hole spacing across X (short axis)

name: imu_hole_cc_y
note: Breadboard mount hole spacing along Y (long axis)

name: imu_screw_tap_dia
note: Thread-form pilot in the breadboard standoffs. M3 assumed -- a 38.1 x 50.8 board on this hole pattern normally carries 3.2 mm holes. Set to 1.7 if the board measures M2

name: imu_pos_x
note: Breadboard centre X **on the Pi-M shelf**. On the centreline: the offset to 35 existed only to clear the battery bay ring on the tub floor
column7: and off the floor there is nothing to clear. Kills the accelerometer lever-arm term outright

name: imu_pos_y
note: Breadboard centre Y on the shelf
column7: aft of the Pi board. Sits between two fixed neighbours: 4.1 mm behind the Pi board's aft edge and 3.6 mm ahead of the aft loom slot

name: torso_iface_dy
note: Torso bolt rectangle Y (M3 heat-set; inboard of 90 mm torso depth)

scs_body_h

name: torso_lean

head_w

name: caster_float
note: Roller bottom above the floor at ride height. The tail is a stop

name: caster_wheel_w

name: tail_tyre_lip_h

name: # --- Waist interface reserve (lean-ready for V2 powered waist) ---
# The TPU loop carries a single central row of lugs on its inner face. The drive
# sprocket has matching pockets in its rim; the idler and road wheels have a
# continuous clearance groove and ride the two smooth lands either side of the
# lug row. This decouples road-wheel diameter from the tooth pitch
# row doubles as the anti-derailment guide.
sprocket_teeth
note: Pockets around the drive sprocket rim; sets lug pitch = pi*sprocket_pitch_dia/sprocket_teeth

name: track_lug_count
note: Lugs around the loop. 29 x 12.566 = 364.42 mm inner path -> straight run 119.38 mm; the idler slot absorbs the 0.62 mm difference from the nominal 120 mm wheelbase and all pretension

name: track_lug_h
note: Lug height above the band inner face

name: track_lug_tip_w
note: Lug width at the tip (across the track)

name: track_lug_chamfer
note: 45 deg self-supporting flare from tip to root. The loop prints with its width vertical so a straight-sided centre lug would start in mid-air; the flare makes it a 45 deg overhang and adds a root fillet where shear is highest

name: lug_clear_r
note: Radial clearance under the lug tip in every wheel groove and sprocket pocket

name: lug_pocket_clear
note: Circumferential clearance on the sprocket pocket

name: lug_side_clear
note: Lateral clearance between lug and groove flank; also the groove's guidance slop

name: wheel_width
note: Common width of sprocket / idler / road wheel; 1 mm inside each track edge

name: wheel_rim_wall
note: Rim wall left under the groove root

name: wheel_hub_od
note: Hub outer dia; 3 mm of material around a 623ZZ seat

name: wheel_spokes
note: Full-width spokes tying hub to rim. Through-features only: with the wheel axis vertical every face is a vertical wall
column7: so the wheels print with no support at all

name: bearing_seat_fit
note: Diametral interference on printed bearing seats (negative = press)

name: sprocket_collar_od
note: Set-screw collar OD; lives in the 3 mm gap between the tub wall outer face and the sprocket inboard face

name: sprocket_journal_len
note: ø6 journal inboard of the collar; 2.8 mm of it in the MR106ZZ and 2 mm running as a plain land in the wall slug

name: motor_shaft_flat_half
note: Half-width of the D-shaft flat plus clearance. Torque goes through the flat; the grub screw only stops the sprocket walking off the shaft

name: drive_hub_clear
note: Wall slug bore around the ø6 journal. Was 6.6 (free clearance); at 6.2 the slug adds 2 mm of plain-bearing length ahead of the MR106ZZ and shortens the sprocket overhang

name: axle_collar_od

name: idler_boss_t
